items.title: Andrej Karpathy: AGI is still a decade away
items.creator: Dwarkesh Podcast, with Andrej Karpathy
items.topic: limits of today's agents and reinforcement learning
items.description: Karpathy explains why agents still lack continual learning and reliable computer use, why he calls RL 'sucking supervision through a straw', and what a small 'cognitive core' model could be.
items.why_recommended: A builder's honest list of what is missing in current agents. Each gap is a possible research question.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A clear map of open problems in agents, memory and learning from experience.

items.title: But how do AI images and videos actually work? | Guest video by Welch Labs
items.creator: 3Blue1Brown, guest video by Welch Labs
items.description: A visual walk through how diffusion models turn noise into images and video, how text guides them, and the geometry behind the steps.
items.why_recommended: The clearest visual intuition for diffusion I know of. Good for explaining generative models to others too.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A picture in your head of what a diffusion model is doing at each step.

items.title: Circuits Updates: October 2026 (The J++ Lens)
items.creator: Anthropic interpretability team and Anthropic Fellows
items.topic: interpretability lenses for reading latent variables
items.description: An improved Jacobian lens that clusters activations at each layer and fits a separate readout per cluster. The authors report it finds reasoning-related latent variables more reliably, with code and a demo.
items.why_recommended: A short, concrete method note with released code. Easy to try on a small model.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A new tool for reading what a model represents mid-computation.

items.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
items.creator: Konstantin Kakaes, Quanta Magazine
items.topic: AI-generated proofs and how humans check them
items.description: An AI system produced a proof that all nontrivial zeta zeros have real part between 1/12 and 11/12. Number theorists are still checking it, and they disagree on when to call it a theorem.
items.why_recommended: A real case study in evaluating AI output when the answer is hard to verify.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A feel for what trust and verification mean when AI does research.

items.title: 339 | Ned Block on Whether Consciousness Requires Biology
items.creator: Sean Carroll's Mindscape, with Ned Block
items.description: Philosopher Ned Block explains why the Turing Test cannot settle consciousness, separates experience from access to information, and argues that how a system computes may matter, not only what it outputs.
items.why_recommended: It questions an assumption many in AI take for granted: that the same behaviour means the same mind.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: Sharper words for talking about whether AI systems could be conscious.

cross_domain.connection: Block's point that the implementation of a computation may matter links to interpretability: we study how models compute, not just what they output.

items.title: How M.C. Escher's Art Creates Bizarre Mathematical Worlds
items.creator: Shalma Wegsman, Quanta Magazine
items.topic: symmetry, tilings and hyperbolic space in Escher
items.description: Escher had no maths training, yet his tilings, Circle Limit prints and Print Gallery inspired mathematicians. Written around a new MoMath exhibition in New York, open until February 2027.
items.why_recommended: Beautiful pictures that teach real geometry: the 17 symmetry groups and hyperbolic space.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: An intuition for symmetry groups and curved space, through art.

items.title: The Surprising Power of Questions
items.creator: Alison Wood Brooks and Leslie K. John, Harvard Business Review
items.description: Research on why questions build trust and learning, with five habits: ask follow-ups, use open questions well, order questions with care, pick the right tone, and mind the group.
items.why_recommended: Follow-up questions are the simplest habit here, and research shows they make people like you more.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: One small habit to try in your next conversation: ask one more follow-up.

items.title: What we can't measure about AI, yet
items.creator: Carlo Cordasco, Aeon
items.topic: why the benefits of new technology are hard to see
items.description: Costs of new inventions are easy to list, but their biggest benefits often stay invisible at first. Cases from anaesthesia, the phonograph and electric light, applied to AI.
items.why_recommended: History makes a point about evaluation: what we can measure is not all that matters.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: Historical examples of hidden benefits, and a case for reversible experiments.

items.title: Tokyo Story (1953)
items.creator: Yasujiro Ozu, with a BFI guide to the film
items.description: An elderly couple visit their busy grown-up children in Tokyo. A quiet, deeply moving film about family and change. The BFI piece explains its style. It contains spoilers, so read it after.
items.why_recommended: Often named among the greatest films ever made, and a gentle way into Japanese life and cinema.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A slow, moving evening and a feel for Ozu's calm, low-camera style.

items.title: Tristan da Cunha: The busiest place you've never seen
items.creator: NPR, Nick Schönfeld and Julia Gunther
items.topic: life on the most remote inhabited island
items.description: A photo story about the 221 people in one village on a South Atlantic island, where everyone does several jobs. It covers the 1817 founding agreement and the 1961 volcano evacuation.
items.why_recommended: A beautiful visual story about how a tiny, isolated community works together.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A picture of a place almost no one visits, and how isolation shapes cooperation.

items.title: The female botanist who sweetened a nation
items.creator: Mandeep Matharu, Royal Horticultural Society
items.description: Janaki Ammal, born in Kerala in 1897, bred sweeter sugarcane for India, co-wrote a chromosome atlas of plants, became the RHS's first woman scientist and helped save Silent Valley.
items.why_recommended: An inspiring Indian scientist many people have never heard of, whose work still matters.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: The story of a scientist who crossed fields, countries and barriers.

items.title: Watch the Geminid meteor shower (peak 13 to 14 December)
items.creator: EarthSky guide
items.description: The year's best meteor shower peaks on the night of 13 to 14 December. A thin crescent moon sets early, so skies are dark. Best around 2 a.m. Its parent is an asteroid, which is rare.
items.why_recommended: Dark skies this year make it a good chance. Note the date now, nothing else to do yet.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A quiet night outside, and maybe dozens of meteors an hour from a dark spot.
